module_title: Atomic Structure and the Dual Nature of Light
introduction: Modern physics began in the early 20th century when scientists realized that atoms are not indivisible solid spheres, but complex systems containing even smaller particles, and that light behaves in mysterious ways.

core_concepts.title: Subatomic Particles and Discoveries
core_concepts.description:
1. Electron ($e^-$): Negatively charged. Discovered by J.J. Thomson.
2. Proton ($p^+$): Positively charged. Discovered by Ernest Rutherford (Goldstein first observed canal rays, but Rutherford named the proton and discovered the nucleus).
3. Neutron ($n^0$): No charge (neutral). Discovered by James Chadwick.

core_concepts.title: Dual Nature of Light
core_concepts.description:
Light has a dual nature. It travels as an Electromagnetic Wave, but it interacts with matter as tiny packets of energy called 'Photons'. 
Energy of a photon: $E = h\nu$ (where $h$ is Planck's constant and $\nu$ is frequency).

core_concepts.title: Photoelectric Effect
core_concepts.description: When light of a certain frequency falls on a metal surface, it knocks electrons out of the metal. This proved the 'particle nature' of light. Albert Einstein successfully explained this phenomenon.

important_entities.name: Einstein's Nobel Prize
important_entities.significance: Albert Einstein won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his discovery of the law of the Photoelectric Effect, NOT for his famous Theory of Relativity ($E=mc^2$). This is a highly repeated exam question.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: J.J. Thomson discovered the electron, but Ernest Rutherford discovered the central 'Nucleus' of the atom through his famous 'Gold Foil Alpha-Scattering Experiment'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Proton -> Rutherford. Electron -> Thomson. Neutron -> Chadwick.

exam_strategy_tips: SSC Direct Question: 'Which subatomic particle has zero mass and zero charge?' Answer: The Photon (or Neutrino, depending on options. But Neutrons have mass!).
